stories.headline: Suspected ShinyHunters Member Detained in Jordan and Assisting FBI
stories.in_brief: A suspected ShinyHunters hacker, identified as Saif al‑Din Khader, was detained in Jordan and is cooperating with U.S. authorities. The group previously claimed a breach of FBI systems that allegedly exposed terabytes of data.
stories.so_what: The detention of a known ShinyHunters affiliate could provide law‑enforcement agencies with insider knowledge of the extortion group’s infrastructure, potentially leading to further arrests and disruption of its operations. ShinyHunters has asserted that it exploited an alleged Oracle PeopleSoft zero‑day to infiltrate FBI networks and later moved laterally into AWS GovCloud, claiming to have exfiltrated 2–3 TB of sensitive information. While the FBI has confirmed an investigation, it has not verified the scale of the alleged data loss. The arrest follows a recent capture of a Dutch suspect linked to the same group, indicating a coordinated international effort to dismantle the cyber‑crime network. Observers will watch for additional disclosures from the FBI and any further disruptions to ShinyHunters’ online presence, which may signal the group’s weakening or a shift in tactics.
stories.what_to_do:
- Apply any available patches for Oracle PeopleSoft and related systems.
- Review and tighten access controls on AWS GovCloud accounts.
- Rotate credentials and monitor for suspicious activity on accounts that may have been exposed.

claims.quote: Rey, whose real name is Saif al-Din Khader, is said to have been brought into custody on September 29, 2026, cooperating with the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and law enforcement to identify other members of the group.

claims.quote: In September, ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer that it breached FBI systems using an alleged Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability before spreading laterally into FBI-managed AWS GovCloud systems.

stories.headline: Warlock ransomware group exploits SharePoint flaws to disable security tools and deploy ransomware
stories.in_brief: The China-linked Warlock group leveraged multiple Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities, including the ToolShell zero‑days, to gain initial access, disable security software on dozens of hosts, and deploy ransomware. The campaign has hit critical infrastructure and other organizations in Portuguese‑ and Spanish‑speaking countries, highlighting ongoing risks from unpatched SharePoint deployments.
stories.so_what: The attacks demonstrate that the ToolShell chain of SharePoint vulnerabilities (CVE‑2025‑49704, CVE‑2025‑49706, CVE‑2025‑53770, CVE‑2025‑53771) remains an effective entry point for threat actors, even months after their disclosure. By using a BYOVD technique with the signed K7RKScan driver (CVE‑2025‑1055), the group can quickly disable AV/EDR solutions on at least 40 machines, allowing rapid ransomware spread to at least 33 hosts via the domain’s SYSVOL share. Targeting water utilities, telecom providers, government bodies and universities across Europe, Africa and Latin America, the campaign underscores the need for organizations with on‑premises SharePoint to apply patches, monitor for unusual driver loading, and restrict the use of legitimate tools such as Visual Studio Code tunneling. Future observations should watch for additional SharePoint‑related exploits and the possible emergence of new BYOVD‑based payloads.
stories.what_to_do: 1. Apply the latest Microsoft patches for SharePoint, including fixes for CVE‑2025‑49704, CVE‑2025‑49706, CVE‑2025‑53770, CVE‑2025‑53771. 2. Audit and block the K7RKScan.sys driver (CVE‑2025‑1055) and other unsigned drivers loaded via BYOVD. 3. Monitor SYSVOL and domain controller activity for unexpected file drops or new services such as VS Code tunneling.

claims.claim: Warlock exploited a chain of zero‑day vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint known as ToolShell (CVE‑2025‑49704, CVE‑2025‑49706, CVE‑2025‑53770, and CVE‑2025‑53771).
claims.quote: The gang emerged in June 2025 and gained notoriety a month later after exploiting a chain of zero‑day vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint known as ToolShell (CVE‑2025‑49704, CVE‑2025‑49706, CVE‑2025‑53770, and CVE‑2025‑53771).

claims.claim: In one intrusion the attackers disabled security software on at least 40 hosts within about two hours and then deployed Warlock ransomware on at least 33 hosts.
claims.quote: According to the researchers, in one intrusion that started on July 22, the threat actor deployed a tool that disabled protection software on “at least 40 hosts within about two hours.” The attacker then launched Warlock ransomware on at least 33 hosts.

claims.claim: The group used the signed K7RKScan driver vulnerable to CVE‑2025‑1055 in a BYOVD attack to kill AV/EDR tools.
claims.quote: Symantec and Carbon Black researchers say that in some attacks attributed to Longlegs, an AV/EDR‑killing tool was deployed via the bring your own vulnerable driver (BYOVD) technique using a signed K7RKScan driver vulnerable to CVE‑2025‑1055.

claims.claim: Victims were water utilities, telecom providers, a regional government body and a university in Portuguese‑ and Spanish‑speaking countries across Europe, Africa and Latin America.
claims.quote: "In the past two months, Longlegs has attacked at least four organizations, including two critical infrastructure operators (a water utility and a telecommunications provider), a regional government body, and a university," the Broadcom‑owned cybersecurity unit said.

stories.headline: Meta launches Muse shopping agent and open‑source hardware kit
stories.in_brief: Meta unveiled its Muse AI agent that can browse retail sites, suggest items and check out for users, and announced an open‑source Muse Gadgets project for developers. The moves expand Muse’s consumer functions and invite third‑party hardware creation.
stories.so_what: Muse’s ability to shop on behalf of users marks a new frontier for AI‑driven commerce, allowing shoppers to specify brands, price and availability before the agent prepares checkout and presents an approval card. Meta will earn a small transaction fee, while partners such as Link by Stripe and Shopify Shop Pay provide payment processing, and PayPal is slated to join later. However, Amazon has blocked Muse from its site, alleging credential storage and data scraping, highlighting privacy concerns that could shape retailer responses. The open‑source Muse Gadgets kit, including free Home Link devices, lets developers attach Muse to custom hardware, potentially extending its reach into small‑business workflows and enterprise platforms. Watch for retailer policy updates, adoption rates of the hardware kit, and any regulatory scrutiny of AI‑mediated purchasing.

stories.headline: Trump appoints intelligence chief Jay Clayton to lead new Super Intelligence Force
stories.in_brief: President Donald Trump announced that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as the White House AI czar and head the newly created Super Intelligence Force. The task force is charged with coordinating federal AI policy and will report to the president within 120 days.
stories.so_what: The appointment places a former SEC chair and Manhattan prosecutor at the helm of the United States' central AI coordination effort, signaling the administration's intent to centralize AI oversight under a single leader. By branding the initiative as a "Super Intelligence Force" and including senior officials from the FTC, the Department of Defense and the Office of Personnel Management as vice chairs, the White House aims to align government agencies, industry, and civil society around its AI agenda. The 120‑day deadline for a risk‑and‑opportunity report suggests an accelerated timeline for policy recommendations, which could shape future regulations, funding priorities, and international competitiveness, especially regarding China. Observers will watch how the force balances innovation with safety, and whether its recommendations translate into binding rules or remain advisory.

stories.headline: Amazon pledges $1 billion for data‑center neighbors and ends NDAs amid backlash
stories.in_brief: Amazon announced a $1 billion five‑year community investment plan and said it will no longer use nondisclosure agreements with government agencies. The moves come as protests and regulatory moratoriums target the company’s expanding data‑center footprint.
stories.so_what: Amazon’s commitments aim to address growing community concerns over the environmental and social impacts of its data centers, which have sparked protests and led several states to consider or enact permit moratoriums. By pledging more than $1 billion for local priorities such as education, job training and water preservation, the company seeks to mitigate opposition and portray its projects as beneficial. Simultaneously, ending NDAs is presented as a transparency measure, responding to activist criticism that secrecy fuels distrust. Observers will watch whether the funding translates into tangible local benefits, how the cessation of NDAs affects government negotiations, and if the announced initiatives influence pending moratoriums, including New York’s one‑year ban on large data‑center permits.

stories.headline: Curiosity rover captures 360° selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge on Mars
stories.in_brief: NASA’s Curiosity rover recorded a 360-degree panoramic selfie at the south rim of Vera Rubin Ridge on sol 1943, corresponding to Jan. 23, 2018. The image combines 61 exposures and marks a total elevation gain of 1 km as of Aug. 26, 2026.
stories.so_what: The selfie demonstrates Curiosity’s continued ability to produce high‑resolution, immersive imagery after more than a decade on Mars, offering scientists and the public a detailed view of the ridge’s geology and surrounding terrain. By stitching together 61 individual shots from the rover’s MAHLI camera, the panorama provides a comprehensive visual context for ongoing studies of the Mount Sharp region. The documented elevation gain of 1 kilometer since the rover’s landing highlights its extensive traverse across Gale Crater, informing future mission planning and comparative analysis with upcoming Mars explorers. Observers will watch for further releases from Curiosity’s imaging suite and any related scientific findings derived from the Vera Rubin Ridge area.

stories.headline: NASA astronaut Christina Koch to appear at Philadelphia NFL game
stories.in_brief: NASA astronaut Christina Koch will attend the Philadelphia Eagles‑Los Angeles Rams game on Oct. 4 as part of the agency’s Inspiration Tour. The appearance highlights NASA’s effort to connect the public with its Artemis Moon‑return program.
stories.so_what: Koch’s participation links a high‑profile sporting event with NASA’s outreach, aiming to raise awareness of the Artemis program and broader U.S. space leadership. By showcasing an astronaut who logged 338 days in space and flew on Artemis II’s historic lunar flyby—the first near‑Moon mission in over half a century—NASA seeks to inspire interest in space exploration among diverse audiences. The Inspiration Tour will continue nationwide, culminating in the MAX POWER exposition at Kennedy Space Center on Nov. 7‑8, which will display next‑generation air and space technologies. Observers will watch how such public‑engagement efforts translate into support for future missions and funding decisions.

stories.headline: G7 agrees to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel following US pressure
stories.in_brief: G7 leaders have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from strategic reserves over four months, with a substantial diesel release in the first 20 days. The move follows pressure from US President Donald Trump, who had threatened to ban US diesel exports unless Europe tapped its own stockpiles.
stories.so_what: The coordinated release is intended to stabilise global fuel markets and lower petroleum product prices, particularly diesel, which affects transport and agriculture costs. The decision follows a G7 agreement ensuring there will be no export restrictions between members. Watch for how quickly the releases are executed and any further adjustments to the volume.
